name: Paintcourt
positioning: Paintcourt is a riso-printed, zine-spirited basketball culture publication that covers the game from the blacktop up: players, sneakers, courts and style, told with the energy of a 90s photocopied fanzine.
audience: Culture-first hoops fans aged 16 to 35 who care as much about the fit, the sneakers and the neighbourhood court as the box score; streetwear collectors, rec-league players and designers.
strategy: Lead with a collectible weekly 'issue' format so every post feels like a page torn from a zine, not a scoreboard update. Pair editorial features with community moments (court repaints, sneaker anatomy, data zines) so the brand earns a place both online and on the court. Every story is clearly labelled as a fictional sample story for this concept brand.

contrastPairs.use: body text on ink sections and story-format creatives
body text on purple color blocks
buttons, highlight bars and text on orange blocks

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; sections breathe at 96px desktop / 56px mobile; collage elements deliberately break the grid by 8 to 24px offsets
designSystem.radius: Mostly hard corners (0px) for zine cards; fully rounded pills (999px) reserved for stickers and buttons
designSystem.borders: Chunky 3 to 6px Blacktop Ink outlines, dashed 'cut here' borders for forms and coupons, offset hard shadows (6px 6px 0 ink)
designSystem.imagery: Original flat vector illustration only: court key diagrams, fictional sneaker silhouettes, player cards; halftone dot fills and fractal grain to mimic risograph print
designSystem.shapes: Court key rectangles, free-throw arcs, starbursts, rotated tape strips, circular stamps
designSystem.buttons: Orange or ink blocks with ink outline and hard offset shadow; press state removes the shadow; Rubik Mono One label or bold Space Grotesk caps
designSystem.cards: Cream paper cards with thick ink borders, rotated -2 to +2 degrees, tape strips and SAMPLE STORY stickers; straighten on hover
designSystem.motifs: Court key lines, sneaker silhouettes, sticker collages, risograph halftone textures, rotated labels, bold color blocks

artDirection: Every creative should feel like a page from a photocopied 90s fanzine: one bold color block, one oversized Rubik Mono One headline with an orange highlight bar, and a collage of stickers, tape and court-key linework. Use halftone dots and a light grain overlay for risograph texture; never use photography or real players, teams, leagues or sneaker brands. Rotate supporting labels 2 to 12 degrees, keep headlines straight and legible, and always label editorial content as a fictional SAMPLE STORY.
